clue.text: This place for leader of diocese

definitions.text: This place for leader of diocese

parts.note: this place means here, the spot where we are
taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of diocese is used

explanation.surface: A question about where a bishop should be based.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: Hereford is a cathedral city that gives its name to a diocese, whose leader is its bishop. 'leader of' takes the first letter of 'diocese'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city in the English West Midlands is the seat of an Anglican bishop and names his see.

clue.text: Sort of insect in grain container

definitions.meaning: a grasshopper or leafhopper is a jumping insect
a funnel-shaped bin that feeds grain or coal downwards

explanation.definitionFit: Jumping bugs are called this, and so is the feed bin on a mill or farm.

clue.text: Form of ceremony used by some spiritualists

indicators.note: used by some means some of the letters of the word are taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A ceremonial practice followed by some mediums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by some' takes a run of letters inside 'spiritualists'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual is a set form of religious or ceremonial action.

clue.text: Suitable activity for a tailor

definitions.meaning: a tailor measures and adjusts clothes on a customer during a session

explanation.definitionFit: An adjective meaning apt, and the noun for a dressmaker's try-on session.

clue.text: State should give soldier hand when things go wrong

indicators.note: when things go wrong suggests disorder, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A nation expects a soldier to lend a hand in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when things go wrong' rearranges SOLDIER HAND.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest of the United States, in New England.

clue.text: Pictures and silver in house gone over

indicators.note: in places the metal's symbol inside the turned-round dwelling
gone over suggests something flipped right round, so the word for the house is read backwards

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a common British home
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Artworks and silverware in a home that has been ransacked or inspected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone over' reads the house word backwards as IMES, and 'in' places the metal inside. A semi is a semi-detached house, two homes sharing one wall, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural nouns for visual representations such as paintings or photographs.

clue.text: Girl left at home becomes sentimental

parts.note: Maud is a girl's name
at home means in, as when someone is in rather than out

explanation.surface: A girl abandoned at home turns weepy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Maudlin means tearfully or foolishly emotional, often from drink.

clue.text: Foreign police officer named Reg? That's unlikely!

indicators.note: the exclamation expresses doubt about the name, hinting that its letters should be rearranged

explanation.surface: Scepticism that a French cop could really be called Reg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's unlikely!' rearranges NAMED REG.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a French armed police officer.

clue.text: Judgement given in a series of words

definitions.meaning: a grammatical unit of words, from capital letter to full stop

explanation.definitionFit: A judge passes a punishment ruling, and a written grammatical unit shares the same name.

clue.text: Drink made from vegetable I imbibed before noon

indicators.note: before sets the vegetable piece ahead of the letter for midday
imbibed means drunk in, so the letter goes inside the vegetable word

parts.note: a potato is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A drink brewed from a vegetable, which the speaker swallowed before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibed' puts I inside POTATO, making POTATIO, and 'before' places that ahead of N for noon.
explanation.definitionFit: A potation is a formal or humorous word for an alcoholic beverage or a drinking session.

clue.text: Go to bed — one could be tossin' and this!

definitions.text: one could be tossin' and this!
definitions.meaning: the phrase 'tossing and turning' describes restless sleep; drop the G as the clue does with tossin'

explanation.definitionFit: Retiring for the night is the everyday phrasal-verb sense, and restless sleepers toss and turn in bed.

clue.text: Avoiding woman and first son, I have to hang behind

indicators.note: to hang behind means to trail at the back, so the contraction for I have comes last

parts.note: Eva is a woman's name

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word son

parts.note: I have contracts to I've, giving these letters

explanation.surface: Someone dodging a woman and her eldest boy, choosing to lag behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes only the opening letter of 'son'; 'to hang behind' puts the contraction of 'I have' at the very end, trailing the woman and son.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasive means dodging or sidestepping, as a slippery answer does.

clue.text: Rob, unwell, grabbed by attendant

indicators.note: grabbed by means held inside, so the word for sick sits within the servant word

parts.note: a page is a young attendant or servant
unwell means ill

explanation.surface: A sick person has their pocket picked by a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbed by' sets the sickness word inside the servant word. 'Rob' looks like a man's name opening the clue, but it is the verb and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillage means to plunder or loot, as invading soldiers did.

clue.text: Role given to company head to get in on the act

parts.note: a role is a part in a play
ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a major British company
pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: An actor is cast at the firm's top level so as to join the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI was a big British chemicals firm, Imperial Chemical Industries; 'head' is PATE, not a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To join in or take part, the idiom being to get involved.

clue.text: Possibly most organic food is, if it's good

definitions.text: Possibly most organic food is, if it's good

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the following words may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A claim that organic produce is the best eating, provided it tastes good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' signals an anagram of MOST ORGANIC; the whole clue is also the definition, describing good food as fine dining.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the art and enjoyment of fine eating, so excellent food earns it.

clue.text: Jingoists at scene of disorder nabbed by police sergeant

indicators.note: nabbed by means arrested and held, so the words sit inside the officer's abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
a riot is a scene of public disorder

explanation.surface: Flag-waving nationalists arrested at a riot by a sergeant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nabbed by' places the preposition and the disturbance together inside the officer's two-letter abbreviation, as if the sergeant had arrested them.
explanation.definitionFit: Jingoists are aggressive nationalists, a fierce kind of loyal citizen.

clue.text: One little man's seen with another in airport

parts.note: Stan, short for Stanley, is a man's name in its diminutive form, here with a possessive
Ted, short for Edward, is another such name

explanation.surface: One short chap is spotted with another in a terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals pet forms of names: STAN for Stanley, TED for Edward. STANSTED is a London airport in Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: London Stansted is one of the capital's main air terminals.

clue.text: Noisy disagreement with Conservative caught in change

indicators.note: caught in means trapped inside, so the party letter goes within the word for change

parts.note: an alteration is a change
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British political party

explanation.surface: A row breaks out when a Tory is snagged by a policy shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in' drops the party letter into the middle of the word for change, just after its first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a heated quarrel or shouting match.

clue.text: Engineers given tenure free

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
a lease is a tenure of property

explanation.surface: Army engineers are granted a rent-free tenancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like an adjective about the tenure; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To release is to set loose or liberate.

clue.text: Iron container knocked over with smart blow

indicators.note: knocked over means tipped upside down, so the container word is read backwards

parts.note: a bin is a container
a lick is a sharp blow, as in a lick of a whip

explanation.surface: A metal bin is toppled with a sharp strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns BIN into NIB. 'Iron' is a golf club: the niblick was an old lofted iron, like today's nine-iron.
explanation.definitionFit: The niblick was the old name for a lofted golf club, roughly a modern nine-iron.

clue.text: Servant with short skirt on

parts.note: a mini is a miniskirt

explanation.surface: A maid wearing a miniskirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A minion is a lowly, obsequious follower or underling.

clue.text: Sin of female leading to death

indicators.note: leading to puts the first pieces ahead of the word for death

parts.note: end means death

explanation.surface: A woman's wrongdoing ends in her demise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading to' puts the preposition and the letter for female in front of the word for death; 'of' is used just as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to transgress or do wrong, as against a law or moral code.

clue.text: Was first to pursue row and caused irritation

indicators.note: to pursue means to follow, so the word for led comes after the row word

parts.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers or taxis
someone who was first led the field

explanation.surface: Someone who came first after a quarrel left a lingering grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pursue' means the 'was first' word follows the 'row' word. 'row' tempts as a quarrel to match the irritation, but here it is a line, as of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rankled is the past tense of to fester and annoy, as a slight does over time.

clue.text: Where barrister may expect to find summary of facts shortly

definitions.text: Where barrister may expect to find summary of facts
definitions.meaning: a barrister's brief is the summary of a case's facts, so the facts are found inside it
shortly means in a few words, briefly

explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer receives a written summary called a brief, and the phrase also means concisely.

clue.text: Away from home bet there will be expenses

parts.note: away from home means out, as a team playing an away match
to lay is to place a bet

explanation.surface: Wagering on an away game is bound to cost money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bet' is the verb LAY, as in laying odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlay is money spent on something, its cost or expenditure.

clue.text: Mad Rita in form of drama at the seaside

indicators.note: in places the jumbled name inside the drama word

parts.note: mime is a form of drama performed without words

indicators.note: mad suggests something deranged, so the letters of the name are scrambled

explanation.surface: A crazy woman named Rita performing a play beside the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' scrambles the name into ARIT, and 'in' sets that after the first letter of the drama word, splitting it open.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime means relating to or bordering the sea, as coastal towns are.

clue.text: Beginning to see snake makes one less happy

indicators.note: beginning to points at the opening letter of the next word only

parts.note: an adder is a snake, Britain's only venomous one

explanation.surface: Glimpsing a snake upsets someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to' takes S from 'see'; 'makes one' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadder is the comparative of unhappy, so it means more gloomy.

clue.text: A man into marijuana becomes debilitated

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the article and the name sit within the drug word

parts.note: weed is slang for marijuana
Ken is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man who has got into cannabis grows feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' sets the article and the man's name inside the cannabis word, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Weakened means made feeble or sapped of strength.
